_readme: Where each Legend stands in the new-build pass (owner 2026-09-05: 'I'll
want this same for all remaining legends. Not in the 9.'). Hand-kept,
because the last stage is his ear and nothing can derive that.
stage:  not started | researched | built | auditioned | confirmed
confirmed means HE HAS HEARD IT AND SAID YES. Nothing else
verdict: his actual words, so the next session doesn't re-litigate it.

Doc Day.verdict: I like b from the new audition. The kick sounds good.
Doc Day.notes: First one. Four research changes (dry snare, working sub under the kick via allow_peak_db, transient shaping, ratio 4.0 bus compression) + own_soundbank + kit tags rewritten to words that match real filenames + snare_locked_24. Took three audition batches to get one he could judge; the first two rendered the config skeleton instead of calling compose().

Razor.notes: Rendered and measured, NOT heard. Nine changes, all in his block only: allow_dirt (his SP-1200 dust 0.6, vinyl -38, wow and 1.35 drive had NEVER played once - clean_renders stripped all of it), wow 0.2->0.5, mix_sat 0->1.5 and kick_dist 0->3.0 ('console into the red'), his own mix_eq with the air CUT to -1.5 dB at 8 kHz (SP-1200 Nyquist ~13 kHz - the era could not make air), space gated->room, jitter 6->8 on kick and snare, kit tags + kick_flavors rewritten to words that match real filenames, own_soundbank on, stamp LANE dropped (owner call - clang/gong/sword matched 1 fx file in 356). glue deliberately LEFT at 1.8, the opposite of Doc Day, because his sources say 'forget about compression, its huge eq work'. Measured new vs old: air -10.3 dB, sub +0.7 dB, attack -1.2 dB. The `roomy` kick tag was in the first render and pulled - it matched Cloud_Roomy_Kick n Hat, a compound one-shot with a hat baked in. Caught by reading the printed sample list.

Mustang.notes: Rendered and measured, NOT heard. He was already CLEAN and his line says 'clean digital', so unlike Razor there was no grime to switch on - the July rule agrees with him. Changes: allow_dirt 'low' + kick_dist 9.0 (808 distorted, mix untouched - owner's call, amount measured over a 4/6/9/12/16 sweep because 4.0 was inaudible); kick jitter 1->3 ms on the KICK LANE ONLY (owner's call, the one place his sources and his own description disagree); the and-of-two kick weight 4->8, which his listen line names and his grammar did not deliver; kit tags fixed and own_soundbank on. HEADLINE: his 'Hey!' chant - the thing Billboard names as his single identifying feature - was pointed at the FX bucket, zero matches in 356 files, while the vox bucket literally contains 'Cymatics - Hey Vox'. Role fx->vox; he is now locked to WUH.wav. Two engine faults fixed on the way: lock_stamps ignored own_soundbank, and the render script crashed on any legend with a clap instead of a snare.

Farrow.notes: Rendered and measured, NOT heard. This one was not a tuning pass: Farrow was a DUPLICATE of Glass Cat, one of the nine — same 98 bpm, same five lanes, same kit tags word for word, same 18 ms clap flam, both 'built' on The Neptunes / Pharrell. Owner: 'I have a version of him in the 9 I want to keep. I want this build to be a different era than that', and 'Nerd'. So Glass Cat keeps the Neptunes minimal era and Farrow is now N.E.R.D. — which is documented, not invented: they withdrew In Search Of... in 2002 and reissued it re-recorded with a live band, and Pharrell's stated reason was that N.E.R.D. 'was to be an entirely different venture ... the band's music should also sound different'. Changes: clap lane DROPPED (his call, 'give it to Glass Cat alone' — the flam is the Neptunes trait and the loudest reason they sounded alike); HAT lane added, closed/tite/ride, because a rock kit has a hi-hat and the snap-instead-of-hats is Glass Cat's; snap demoted from timekeeper to colour; kick/snare/hat jitter to 3 ms (Coleman: Pharrell plays a kit and they loop 16 bars, 'that's where a lot of the feel comes from'; Hugo 2003: 'Pharrell's playing drums'); the 10% 808 kick branch dropped as the OTHER era's drum machine; kit tags fixed and own_soundbank on; chord_source bell->GUITAR (112 real samples, unused by any legend, and 'live drums and guitars' is quoted). Dirt asked and answered: stay completely clean. HEADLINE FAULT: his producer tag was 'Cymatics - LIFE - Rain and Windchimes 4.wav', a field recording of rain on every beat he ever made, because the open bank wiped his tags; now Drip 2.wav. Two script faults fell out: make_legend_newbuild forced BOTH versions to use the new kit, so a structure-only build rendered byte-identical files (its own 'nothing moved' guard caught it) and then crashed on the lane mismatch — fixed with a --structure mode. LEFT INCONSISTENT ON PURPOSE: the rest of his signature harmony block is still written for the classic-minimal era, and Glass Cat still carries the same dead tags (he is one of the nine, out of scope, owner said keep him).

Kane East.notes:
He was a DUPLICATE, not out of tune. Sunday Chop in the nine is also built='Kanye West' and the two listen lines were nearly the same sentence — same 57% swing, same driving pushed kicks, same BIG clap with the snare tucked underneath, same tambourine offbeats. Second legend/crew duplicate found the same day (Farrow was a copy of Glass Cat); the legends and the nine are audited separately, which is how both survived. Owner asked directly, then chose the era: Yeezus, over 808s & Heartbreak and Dark Fantasy. Sunday Chop keeps chipmunk soul and was NOT touched.
Rebuilt as the industrial era: bpm 90->130, swing 57->50, jitter 2->0 on kick/clap/snare, the BIG-clap-over-tucked-snare inverted to a stacked 0.8/0.8, tambourine+shaker perc replaced by 84 real toms at 0.55, gated reverb -> dry, allow_dirt True with kick_dist 6.0 and mix_sat 3.0, and the 30% 808 kick_flavors branch dropped. dust 0.35 -> 0.0 and vinyl -44 -> -80: his old line promised a vinyl bed that had never once played, and the honest fix was to stop promising it, not to finally switch a soul-era bed on under an industrial record. Melodic side moved from strings/choir/gospel to synth/pluck/chip and static minor vamps; library tags from soul/motown to electro/house/punk/drill/minimal/techno.
Dead tags found and fixed before own_soundbank went on, in that order: kick 'warm' 0 files, clap 'big' 0, stamp 'vocal' 0 and 'soul' 0, and 'boom' on the kick matched 3 files of which 2 were 808s.
FOURTH WRONG PRODUCER TAG IN FOUR LEGENDS: his locked stamp was 'Cymatics - LIFE - River - Light 4.wav', a field recording of a river, riding every beat he had ever made. Cleared and re-picked to 'wierd ass siren.wav' — Slant Magazine's description of the record names 'slowly morphing drones and sirens' outright. The stamp tags were first written siren/alarm/riser/white-noise (20 files), the lock landed on a white-noise sweep, and they were narrowed to siren/alarm (7) because a riser is not a producer tag.
SCRIPT FIX, and the most reusable thing here: tools/make_legend_newbuild.py now prints the locked stamp at the head of its sample list. build_kit puts it in kit['stamp'] but never in `sources`, so the one sample heard on every single beat was the one sample the 'read the list before you ship it' step could not show. That blind spot is exactly how four wrong producer tags in a row got past it.
Structure build, so a and b share neither a beat nor a tempo (90 vs 130) and the dB numbers compare two different beats: sub -9.37 dB, air +9.20 dB, attack +1.23 dB. The sub drop is intended and documented (short hard kicks, no 808) but it is the biggest single number in the build and it is the thing to listen for.
NOT heard. Only his ear closes it.
